column1: # Case handling, spec §3.7. The engine never folds case: every letter keeps the case
# of the key that produced it, a modifier changes no case at all, and a doubling undo
# puts back the letter as it was typed. `auto_restore` returns the raw keys, so a
# restored word keeps its case by construction.
# A tone key marks a letter; it does not set its case. `aS` and `AS` mark the same `a`
# and differ only in the vowel's case.
# A letter modifier marks the letter in front of it, so the first letter of the pair
# decides: `Aa` and `aA` both mark the first `a`.
# `w`, `[` and `]` produce a letter of their own, so their key case is the letter's
# case where the key has one.
# The struck `d` keeps the case of the `d` it marks.
# Doubling undoes the modifier and keeps the case of the letter on screen; where the
# undo leaves a key behind, that key is the one that undid the mark (`aww → aw`) or the
# one it replaced when nothing was marked (`ww → w`).
# Doubling a tone key and `z` give the tone key's letter back, in the case it was
# typed: the same key with shift held is still the same key.
# Words in the four cases a user types: lower, Title, upper, and a capital somewhere
# inside. The capital stays on the letter it was typed on.
# `auto_restore` gives the raw keys back, case included.
